issues.summary: The sustainability listing, Stegra announcement and linked sustainability.google page are retrieved public corporate disclosures. They do not identify measurable goals, a comparable baseline/progress series or operational hosting evidence specifically for the News from Google publication at blog.google. The Stegra text attributes up to 95% production-emissions reductions to a Stegra estimate; up to 40% embodied-carbon reduction is a Google estimate for data-center infrastructure materials. EAC purchasing and a 2025 construction-project count are publisher statements, not independent blog footprint measurements.
issues.requestedChange: Keep the exact publication-specific sustainability-goals assessmentScope and cantTell for service-specific disclosure/goals/hosting. Attribute corporate estimates and retain their industrial, construction and temporal boundaries if discussed. Request one publication-specific impact statement and goal/progress record; request a dated provider/service relationship to blog.google before judging sustainable hosting. Never transfer the steel percentages to page-load or annual browsing savings.

issues.summary: Root and well-known carbon.txt returned 404 with no Carbon-Location header or usable declared relationships in the frozen discovery. Six retrieved document records include corporate material and an RSS response; this count is not six verified sustainability policies. No parseable carbon file was available for syntax/schema assessment.
issues.requestedChange: State missing carbon.txt within the tested discovery scope only. Do not infer absence of corporate sustainability work, high emissions or failure of all WSG 3.13 from that result. A new delegated record needs an explicit origin relationship and independently corroborated claims.

issues.summary: The pre-submission newsletter page requests one visible required email-address field with a weekly-news purpose, privacy-policy link and stated opt-out. This supports proportionality for the declared visible sign-up scope. No email was entered, no subscription/verification completed and no opt-out was exercised; the broad corporate privacy excerpt cannot verify publication-specific retention, downstream deletion or execution of unsubscribe.
issues.requestedChange: A scoped visible-form pass may cite the required email control and purpose text while retaining the exact assessmentScope and pre-submission boundary. Attribute opt-out as a stated choice, avoid claiming successful delivery/unsubscription or complete processing compliance, and do not request internal source merely to resolve this visible-form check.

issues.summary: The publication about page explains authorship and purpose; the listing and September 17, 2026 announcement show current publication and older content routes. These records do not document a review/expiry schedule or an applied archive/update/deletion decision with rationale. Publication date and continuing availability alone do not establish a lifecycle practice or justify removal of an announcement with historical value.
issues.requestedChange: Keep content-lifecycle cantTell for the declared collection. Request one public correction/update/archive example and the applicable review trigger or schedule, decision rationale and resulting live/historical routes. Do not label old announcements wasteful merely for remaining discoverable.

issues.summary: The recorded desktop pointer journey reaches the canonical Stegra article with its complete heading and body. The sole visible cookie-notice button says OK, got it; the accept class name is an implementation identifier, not proof of an accept/reject preference model or informed analytics consent. The route is an auditor walkthrough and excludes keyboard-only, constrained-device and geographic completion.
issues.requestedChange: Use actual URL/headline/content completion for a bounded access-barriers pass and preserve its exact assessmentScope. Describe cookie action as acknowledgment; do not invent reject/accept parity or infer legal compliance from the notice. Any stronger preference judgment needs a separately captured control/state path, and broader accessibility needs a linked new assessment.
